title: Reply/quote messages
description:
## Description

Tap a message to reply to it. Show quoted original message above the reply in the bubble. Thread context without full threading -- keeps it simple like iMessage/Telegram replies.

### Implementation

**types.ts:**
- Add optional `replyTo` field to `ChatMessage`:
  - `replyTo?: { id: string; username: string; english: string; pigLatin: string }`
  - english and pigLatin are truncated previews, max ~80 chars + ellipsis
- Both english AND pigLatin stored because difficulty modes need different views:
  - Explorer/own messages: show English quote
  - Detective/Spy: show pig latin quote
- Helper: `truncatePreview(text: string, max?: number): string` -- truncate at word boundary + "..."

**server.ts:**
- Accept `replyTo` in `send-message` event payload
- **No validation of replyTo.id** -- the 100-msg buffer does not cover full history, so validation would incorrectly reject replies to older messages. Store as-is; if the original is gone, the quote still shows the preview text.
- Store in SQLite: new nullable JSON column `reply_to` on `messages` table
- DB migration: `ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN reply_to TEXT` (JSON string, nullable)
- Include `replyTo` in `new-message` broadcast and `message-history` (parse JSON from DB)

**socket-context.tsx:**
- Extend `sendMessage` to accept an options object for forward-compatibility with future additions (image, etc):
  - `sendMessage(opts: { english: string; pigLatin: string; replyTo?: ReplyTo })`
  - **Breaking change** from current `sendMessage(english, pigLatin)` signature. Update all call sites (chat-input.tsx).
- Parse `replyTo` from incoming messages into ChatMessage state

**chat-input.tsx:**
- New prop: `replyTarget: ChatMessage | null` + `onClearReply: () => void`
- When `replyTarget` set, show reply bar above input: "Replying to {username}: {preview}..." with X dismiss button
- On send: include replyTo data (truncated previews), then call `onClearReply()`
- Reply bar uses English preview for display (user always sees English in input area)

**message-bubble.tsx:**
- If message has `replyTo`, render quoted block above message content:
  - Light gray background, rounded, small text
  - Show `replyTo.username` (bold) + text preview
  - Text shown depends on context: own messages/Explorer -> english preview; Detective/Spy -> pigLatin preview
- Tap/click on a non-system message bubble calls `onReply(message)` callback
- Tap quoted block scrolls to original message if in view (nice-to-have, not required for exit)

**chat-room.tsx:**
- New state: `replyTarget: ChatMessage | null`
- Wire: MessageBubble `onReply` -> sets replyTarget; ChatInput receives it + onClearReply

### Unit Tests (`src/lib/reply-helpers.test.ts`)

- `truncatePreview("short")` -> `"short"` (no truncation)
- `truncatePreview("a".repeat(100))` -> 80 chars + `"..."`
- Truncation at word boundary, not mid-word
- Empty string -> empty string
- Emoji/special chars preserved in truncation
- ReplyTo object round-trips through JSON.stringify/parse correctly

### E2E Tests (`e2e/reply.test.ts`)

- User A sends "Hello" -> User A taps message -> reply bar appears showing "Hello" preview
- User A types reply text, sends -> reply bubble shows quoted "Hello" above reply content
- User B sees reply with quoted original in their view
- Dismiss reply bar (X button) -> reply target cleared, next send has no quote
- Reply to a long message -> preview truncated with ellipsis
- Reply renders correctly in Explorer mode (English quote shown)
- Reply renders correctly in Spy mode (pig latin quote shown)
- Message history on rejoin preserves reply references
- Reply to system message: should NOT be possible (system messages have no reply tap handler)
- Rapid replies: send reply, immediately tap another message, reply bar updates

### Logging

- E2E: `test.step()` for each action (tap message, verify reply bar, send, verify bubble)
- Log replyTo payload in socket emit
- Screenshot before/after reply send

## Exit Condition

```bash
set -e
cd /Users/thom/10-19_projects/upidstay

# ReplyTo type with both english + pigLatin
grep -qE "replyTo" src/lib/types.ts

# Server stores reply_to
grep -qE "reply_to|replyTo" server.ts

# Message bubble renders quoted original
grep -qE "replyTo|reply-quote" src/components/message-bubble.tsx

# Chat input has reply bar UI
grep -qE "replyTarget|onClearReply" src/components/chat-input.tsx

# sendMessage uses options object
grep -qE "sendMessage.*opts\|sendMessage.*{" src/lib/socket-context.tsx

# Unit tests exist and pass
test -f src/lib/reply-helpers.test.ts
pnpm test -- --reporter=verbose 2>&1 | tee /tmp/1uv-unit.log
grep -qE "truncate|reply|preview" /tmp/1uv-unit.log

# E2E tests exist and pass
test -f e2e/reply.test.ts
pnpm test:e2e -- reply --reporter=list 2>&1 | tee /tmp/1uv-e2e.log
grep -qE "passed|✓" /tmp/1uv-e2e.log

# Build succeeds
pnpm build

rm -f /tmp/1uv-unit.log /tmp/1uv-e2e.log
echo "bd-1uv verified"
```

title: HTTPS for speech-to-text on LAN devices
description:
## Description

Speech recognition API requires secure context. Chromebook on LAN cannot use mic button over plain HTTP.

This is a spike — choose an approach first, then implement.

### Options (evaluate in order of preference)

1. **Cloudflare Tunnel** — zero config HTTPS, requires `cloudflared` daemon. Easiest for LAN access. Free tier sufficient.
2. **mkcert + local CA** — dev-only, must install CA on each device. Good for known device set.
3. **Let's Encrypt + domain** — prod-ready, needs public domain. Overkill for LAN-only use.
4. **Chrome flag workaround** — `chrome://flags/#unsafely-treat-insecure-origin-as-secure`. Fragile, per-device.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Decision documented: which approach chosen and why (in commit message or bead close reason)
2. Implementation complete for chosen approach
3. Dev server accessible over HTTPS on LAN (or secure context equivalent)
4. Chromebook on LAN can activate speech recognition without errors
5. Existing HTTP workflow not broken (HTTPS is additive)
6. Setup documented: any per-device steps clearly listed in README or deploy docs

### Implementation Notes

- PM2 ecosystem config may need updating if tunnel/proxy added
- GitHub Actions deploy script may need tunnel restart step
- Test on actual Chromebook (not just Chrome desktop — different permission model)

## Exit Condition

```bash
set -e
cd /Users/thom/10-19_projects/upidstay

# Some form of HTTPS/secure context config exists
# (exact check depends on chosen approach)
ls cloudflared.yml 2>/dev/null || \
  ls deploy/cloudflared* 2>/dev/null || \
  grep -rqE "https|tls|ssl|cloudflare|mkcert|secure" deploy/ || \
  grep -rqE "https|tls|ssl" server.ts || \
  echo "WARN: No HTTPS config found — verify manually"

# Documentation exists
grep -rqiE "https|secure context|speech|chromebook" README.md 2>/dev/null || \
  grep -rqiE "https|secure context|speech|chromebook" deploy/README.md 2>/dev/null || \
  echo "WARN: No HTTPS documentation found"

# Build still works (no regression)
pnpm build

# Server starts without error
timeout 10 pnpm start &
PID=$!
sleep 6
curl -sf http://localhost:3080 > /dev/null || curl -sf http://localhost:3000 > /dev/null
kill $PID 2>/dev/null

echo "✅ bd-3qg verified (manual Chromebook test still required)"
```

title: S-11.1: Image upload and paste in chat
description: ## Description Support pasting or selecting images to send in chat. Images stored as files on the server (not base64 in DB -- too large). Show inline preview thumbnails in message bubbles. Kid-friendly: no external upload services, everything stays on the local server. ### Implementation **Server-side file handling (server.ts):** The server uses bare `http.createServer` + Next.js handler (NOT Express). Custom routes must intercept requests before passing to Next.js: ```ts const httpServer = createServer(async (req, res) => { if (req.method === 'POST' && req.url === '/api/upload') { // handle upload } else if (req.url?.startsWith('/uploads/')) { // serve static file } else { handle(req, res); // Next.js handler } }); ``` - Use `busboy` (lightweight, stream-based) for multipart parsing -- `pnpm add busboy` + `pnpm add -D @types/busboy` - `POST /api/upload`: accept `multipart/form-data`, single `file` field - Validate MIME type: only `image/jpeg`, `image/png`, `image/gif`, `image/webp` - Max file size: 5MB (reject with 413) - Generate unique filename: `{crypto.randomUUID()}.{ext}` - Save to `data/uploads/` (auto-create dir, gitignore it) - Return JSON: `{ url: "/uploads/{filename}" }` - `GET /uploads/:filename`: serve files from `data/uploads/` with correct Content-Type - Validate filename format (UUID + extension only -- no path traversal) **types.ts:** - Add optional `image` field to `ChatMessage`: `{ url: string; width?: number; height?: number }` - Messages can have text + image, or image only (english/pigLatin may be empty string) **server.ts (socket events):** - Accept optional `imageUrl` in `send-message` payload - Store in SQLite: new nullable `image_url` column on `messages` - DB migration: `ALTER TABLE messages ADD COLUMN image_url TEXT` - Include in broadcast and history **socket-context.tsx:** - If bd-1uv (reply) landed first: extend existing options object with `imageUrl?` - If this lands first: refactor `sendMessage` to options object pattern: `sendMessage(opts: { english: string; pigLatin: string; imageUrl?: string })` Update all call sites. - Image upload is a separate HTTP fetch (not through socket -- binary too large for socket frames) **chat-input.tsx:** - New interactions: - Paperclip button: opens native file picker (`accept="image/jpeg,image/png,image/gif,image/webp"`) - Paste handler: detect image from `event.clipboardData.files` - When image selected/pasted: - Client-side resize: use canvas API to downscale if larger than 1280px on longest side (reduces upload size, saves bandwidth for other users viewing) - Show thumbnail preview above input (below reply bar if both active) - X button to remove before sending - Send flow: resize -> upload via fetch POST -> get URL -> send message with URL - Loading state during upload: disable send button, show spinner on button - Error handling: show inline error message for wrong type or too-large file **message-bubble.tsx:** - If message has `image`, render `` with: - `max-width: 280px`, `max-height: 200px`, `object-fit: contain` - Rounded corners matching bubble style - Loading skeleton (gray placeholder) while image loads - Click to open full-size in new tab (`window.open(url)`) - Image above text (if both present) or alone in bubble - All difficulty modes: image shown as-is (no pig latin transformation of images) ### Unit Tests (`src/lib/image-upload.test.ts`) - Valid MIME types accepted (jpeg, png, gif, webp) - Invalid MIME types rejected (pdf, txt, exe, svg, html) - File size > 5MB rejected - Upload URL format: `/uploads/{uuid}.{ext}` pattern - Path traversal blocked: filenames like `../../../etc/passwd.png` rejected - ChatMessage with image field serializes correctly - ChatMessage without image field backward compatible (existing messages unaffected) - Client-side resize: image > 1280px is downscaled, image < 1280px unchanged ### E2E Tests (`e2e/image-upload.test.ts`) - User selects image via file picker -> thumbnail preview appears above input - User sends -> upload completes -> message with image appears in bubble - User B sees image in real-time - Remove image before sending (X button) -> send is text-only - Paste image from clipboard -> same preview + send flow - Image + text message: both rendered in bubble (image above text) - Image-only message (no text): renders just image in bubble - Oversized file (> 5MB) -> error shown, not sent - Invalid file type (.txt) -> rejected with user-friendly error - Image persists in message history on rejoin - Click image in bubble -> opens full-size in new tab ### Logging - E2E: `test.step()` for file selection, preview, upload, render - Log: upload response status + URL, file size, MIME type - Screenshot: preview state, rendered image in bubble, error states ## Exit Condition ```bash set -e cd /Users/thom/10-19_projects/upidstay # Upload endpoint exists (intercept before Next.js handler) grep -qE "/api/upload" server.ts # busboy or equivalent multipart parser grep -qE "busboy|Busboy|formidable" server.ts pnpm list busboy | grep -q busboy # Static file serving for uploads grep -qE "/uploads" server.ts # Image field in message type grep -qE "image" src/lib/types.ts # Image rendering in message bubble grep -qE "&1 | tee /tmp/o6j1-unit.log grep -qE "image\|upload\|MIME\|resize" /tmp/o6j1-unit.log # E2E tests exist and pass test -f e2e/image-upload.test.ts pnpm test:e2e -- image-upload --reporter=list 2>&1 | tee /tmp/o6j1-e2e.log grep -qE "passed" /tmp/o6j1-e2e.log # Build succeeds pnpm build rm -f /tmp/o6j1-unit.log /tmp/o6j1-e2e.log echo "bd-o6j.1 verified" ```

title: S-11.2: GIF picker integration
description: ## Description Add a GIF search button that lets users search and send GIFs inline. Uses Tenor API (free tier, kid-safe by default). GIF renders as animated image in message bubble, reusing the image field and rendering infrastructure from bd-o6j.1. ### API Choice: Tenor v2 - Free tier: 50 req/s (more than enough for a family chat app) - Kid-safe: `contentfilter=high` parameter filters adult content - No billing required for anonymous API key - Endpoint: `https://tenor.googleapis.com/v2/search?q={query}&key={API_KEY}&contentfilter=high&limit=20&media_filter=tinygif,gif` ### Implementation **Environment:** - New env var: `TENOR_API_KEY` in `.env` and `.env.example` - Server-side proxy to avoid exposing API key to client **server.ts:** - New HTTP routes (intercept before Next.js handler, same pattern as image upload from bd-o6j.1): - `GET /api/gifs?q={query}` -- proxy to Tenor v2 search with server-side API key - `GET /api/gifs/trending` -- trending GIFs for empty search state - `contentfilter=high` enforced server-side (client cannot bypass) - Return simplified response: `{ results: [{ id, preview_url, full_url, width, height }] }` - Rate limit: simple in-memory Map with sliding window (max 10 req/s per client IP) - Missing TENOR_API_KEY: return 503 with helpful error (not crash) **src/components/gif-picker.tsx** (new): - Opens as overlay panel (similar size/style to avatar picker): - Search input at top with debounced fetch (300ms) - Grid of GIF thumbnails (`preview_url` -- smaller/faster loading) - Trending GIFs shown on initial open (before user searches) - Tap GIF to select -> closes picker - Loading skeleton while fetching - "No results" empty state - Close on tap-outside, Escape key, or X button **chat-input.tsx:** - Add GIF button (film/clapper emoji) next to existing buttons - On GIF select: send message with `imageUrl` pointing to Tenor CDN URL (full-size GIF) - No upload needed -- GIFs are external URLs served by Tenor CDN - Text input remains independent (GIF is image-only message) **message-bubble.tsx:** - Already handles `image` field from bd-o6j.1 -- GIF URLs render through same path - Add small "GIF" text badge in corner of image to distinguish from uploaded photos - Animated GIFs play automatically (native browser `` behavior) ### E2E Test Strategy: Mock the API E2E tests MUST NOT hit live Tenor API. Reasons: flaky on network failure, rate limiting, requires API key in CI. Use Playwright `page.route()` to intercept `/api/gifs` and `/api/gifs/trending` requests and return mock responses with predictable data. Test data: 3-4 mock GIF entries with placeholder URLs pointing to static test images in `e2e/fixtures/`. ### Unit Tests (`src/lib/gif-search.test.ts`) - Tenor proxy formats response correctly (mock fetch) - Content filter param always present and set to "high" - Empty query triggers trending endpoint instead of search - Rate limiting: simulate >10 requests -> 429 response - Missing TENOR_API_KEY env -> 503 graceful error - Tenor returns no results -> empty array (not error) ### E2E Tests (`e2e/gif-picker.test.ts`) Uses mocked `/api/gifs` responses (Playwright route interception): - Click GIF button -> picker opens with "trending" GIFs (mocked) - Type search query -> results update after debounce (mocked search response) - Select a GIF -> picker closes -> GIF message appears in chat bubble with "GIF" badge - User B sees GIF in real-time - Clear search -> trending GIFs reappear - Close picker without selecting (Escape) -> no message sent - Close picker without selecting (tap outside) -> no message sent - GIF persists in message history on rejoin - No results state: search for term that returns empty array -> "No GIFs found" displayed ### Logging - E2E: `test.step()` for picker open, search, select, render - Log: search query, mock result count, selected GIF URL - Screenshot: picker with results, GIF rendered in bubble, empty state ## Exit Condition ```bash set -e cd /Users/thom/10-19_projects/upidstay # Tenor API proxy routes grep -qE "/api/gifs" server.ts # Content filter enforced server-side grep -qE "contentfilter" server.ts # GIF picker component test -f src/components/gif-picker.tsx # GIF button in chat input grep -qE "gif\|GIF" src/components/chat-input.tsx # TENOR_API_KEY in env example grep -qE "TENOR_API_KEY" .env.example # Unit tests test -f src/lib/gif-search.test.ts pnpm test -- --reporter=verbose 2>&1 | tee /tmp/o6j2-unit.log grep -qE "gif\|tenor\|content.?filter" /tmp/o6j2-unit.log # E2E tests (with mocked API) test -f e2e/gif-picker.test.ts grep -qE "page.route\|route.*api/gifs" e2e/gif-picker.test.ts pnpm test:e2e -- gif-picker --reporter=list 2>&1 | tee /tmp/o6j2-e2e.log grep -qE "passed" /tmp/o6j2-e2e.log pnpm build rm -f /tmp/o6j2-unit.log /tmp/o6j2-e2e.log echo "bd-o6j.2 verified" ```

title: S-10.2: Change avatar while in chat room
description:
## Description

Add ability to tap your avatar in the chat header to open a picker and switch mid-conversation. Broadcast the change to other room members so it updates in real-time. Avatar change persists to localStorage profile.

### Implementation

**Shared avatar ID list:**
- The AVATARS array lives in `src/lib/types.ts` (client-side). The server currently does NOT import this.
- For server-side validation, extract just the avatar ID set to a shared module OR use a simpler validation: accept any non-empty string as avatarId (the server already stores whatever avatar string the join event provides). The avatar picker UI constrains to valid IDs client-side.
- **Recommended approach**: skip strict server-side validation of avatarId. The server just stores what the client sends. If someone sends garbage via raw socket, worst case they get a fallback emoji (bear). Keep it simple.

**server.ts:**
- New `change-avatar` socket event: `{ avatarId: string }`
- Validate: avatarId is a non-empty string, currentUser and currentRoom exist
- Update user entry in room map: `rooms[roomSlug].users[socketId].avatar = avatarId`
- Broadcast updated `room-users` list to room (same format as join -- triggers existing client-side user list update)
- Do NOT retroactively change past messages -- avatar at time of send is historical

**socket-context.tsx:**
- Expose `changeAvatar(avatarId: string)` function
- Emit `change-avatar` event to server
- Updated room-users listener already handles the refresh (no new listener needed)

**chat-room.tsx:**
- Header: make current user avatar emoji clickable (`aria-label="Change avatar"`)
- On click: show AvatarPicker component as overlay/modal (reuse existing component as-is)
- On avatar select: call `changeAvatar(newId)`, close picker, update localStorage profile
- Close on tap-outside or Escape key

**profiles.ts:**
- New function: `updateProfileAvatar(profileId: string, avatarId: string)` -- update avatar field in localStorage
- Called after avatar change (optimistic -- update local immediately, server broadcast confirms via room-users)

**avatar-picker.tsx:**
- Already exists and works. No changes needed -- reuse as-is in the overlay.

### Unit Tests (`src/lib/avatar-change.test.ts`)

- `updateProfileAvatar` updates correct profile in localStorage
- `updateProfileAvatar` with non-existent profileId is no-op
- Avatar change does not affect other profiles in storage
- Round-trip: change avatar, reload profiles, new avatar persists
- Changing to same avatar is a no-op (no unnecessary write)

### E2E Tests (`e2e/avatar-change.test.ts`)

- User joins room -> clicks header avatar -> AvatarPicker overlay appears
- User selects new avatar -> picker closes -> header shows new avatar emoji
- User B sees User A new avatar in user list in real-time
- User A sends message after change -> new message shows new avatar; old messages keep old avatar
- Avatar persists: User A leaves and rejoins -> avatar is the changed one (localStorage)
- Cancel: open picker, press Escape -> picker closes, avatar unchanged
- Cancel: open picker, click outside -> picker closes, avatar unchanged

### Logging

title: S-10.3: Richer identity display
description:
## Description

Enhance identity display in chat to be more visually distinctive and Telegram-inspired. The codebase already shows avatar emoji + username in message bubbles -- this bead adds **color-coded usernames**, **grouped consecutive messages**, and an optional **profile card on tap**.

### What Already Exists (do NOT reimplement)
- Avatar emoji displayed next to messages
- Username label above messages
- User list in header with avatars

### What Is New

**1. Color-coded usernames:**
- Deterministic color from username string: hash username -> pick hue (0-360) -> `hsl(hue, 70%, 40%)`
- Same user always gets same color across rooms/sessions
- Lightness capped at 40% to ensure WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) against white bubble backgrounds
- Helper: `getUsernameColor(username: string): string` in new `src/lib/username-color.ts`
- Pure function, no side effects

**2. Grouped consecutive messages (message clustering):**
- When same user sends multiple messages in a row (within 2 min), collapse avatar + username -- only show on first message in cluster
- Subsequent messages in cluster have reduced top margin (tight grouping, ~2px gap vs normal ~12px)
- Timestamp shown on last message in cluster (or on hover)
- System messages (join/leave, username="") always break clusters
- Logic extracted to `src/lib/message-clustering.ts` as a pure function:
  `computeClusters(messages: ChatMessage[]): ClusterInfo[]` where ClusterInfo = `{ isFirst: boolean; isLast: boolean }`
  This makes it unit-testable without React rendering.

**3. Profile card on tap (mini):**
- Tap username or avatar in a message -> shows mini profile popover
- Contents: large avatar emoji (3x size), username (colored), "Joined {relative time}" (derived from first message timestamp in current room state)
- Dismiss on tap-outside or Escape key
- No new server data needed -- derive join time from message history

### Implementation Files

**src/lib/username-color.ts** (new):
- `getUsernameColor(username: string): string`
- Simple hash: sum char codes, mod 360 for hue, return `hsl(hue, 70%, 40%)`

**src/lib/message-clustering.ts** (new):
- `computeClusters(messages: ChatMessage[]): ClusterInfo[]`
- Pure function, returns parallel array of `{ isFirst, isLast }` flags
- Rules: same username + within 120s of previous + neither is system message

**src/components/message-bubble.tsx:**
- Apply `getUsernameColor` to username label style
- Accept `isFirstInCluster` and `isLastInCluster` props
- If not first: hide avatar + username, reduce top margin
- If last: show relative timestamp (e.g. "2:34 PM")
- Tap username/avatar -> `onShowProfile(message)` callback (only on first-in-cluster or standalone)

**src/components/chat-room.tsx:**
- Call `computeClusters(messages)` before rendering
- Pass cluster info to each MessageBubble
- Manage profile card state: `profileTarget: ChatMessage | null`
- Render ProfileCard popover positioned near tap point

**src/components/profile-card.tsx** (new):
- Popover component: large avatar, colored username, join time
- Positioned absolutely near the tap point
- Close on outside click or Escape
- Framer Motion fade-in animation

### Unit Tests

**`src/lib/username-color.test.ts`:**
- Same username always returns same color (deterministic)
- Different usernames return different colors (test 10+ names, verify >= 5 distinct hues)
- Empty string returns a valid color without crash
- Returns valid CSS `hsl()` string (regex match)
- All generated colors have lightness <= 45% (contrast safety)

**`src/lib/message-clustering.test.ts`:**
- Single message: `[{ isFirst: true, isLast: true }]`
- 3 messages from same user within 2min: first=true on #1, last=true on #3, middle has both false
- Messages from different users: each is own cluster (all isFirst+isLast true)
- System message (username="") breaks cluster even from same "user"
- Gap > 2min between same user: separate clusters
- Mixed: A, A, B, A -> three clusters (A*2, B*1, A*1)
- Empty array: returns empty array

### E2E Tests (`e2e/identity.test.ts`)

- User sends 3 messages quickly -> avatar/username only shown on first, all three tightly grouped
- Two users alternate messages -> each message has avatar + colored username
- Same username has same color after page reload (deterministic hash)
- Tap username -> profile card appears with avatar + colored name
- Tap outside profile card -> dismisses
- Different users have visibly different name colors (screenshot for visual comparison)
- System messages break clustering: A sends 2, B joins, A sends 1 -> three clusters

### Logging

- E2E: `test.step()` per action
- Log: computed color for each username, cluster groupings array
- Screenshot: clustered messages, profile card visible

## Exit Condition

grep -qE "getUsernameColor" src/lib/username-color.ts

# Message clustering utility

# Unit tests exist and pass
test -f src/lib/username-color.test.ts

pnpm test -- --reporter=verbose 2>&1 | tee /tmp/ssj3-unit.log

title: S-9.1: Room name slugification utility
description:
## Description

Create `src/lib/slugify.ts` exporting `slugifyRoom(name: string): string`.

Rules:
- Lowercase, trim whitespace
- Replace spaces with hyphens
- Strip non-alphanumeric chars (except hyphens)
- Strip emoji (Unicode > U+FFFF)
- Collapse multiple consecutive hyphens
- Idempotent (slugifying a slug returns same slug)
- Throw on empty/whitespace-only input

Create `src/lib/slugify.test.ts` with ≥ 8 test cases:
- `"Rainbow Party!"` → `"rainbow-party"`
- `"hello world"` → `"hello-world"`
- `"  spaces  "` → `"spaces"`
- `"UPPERCASE"` → `"uppercase"`
- `"special@#chars!"` → `"specialchars"`
- `"emoji 🎉 room"` → `"emoji-room"`
- `"already-slugged"` → `"already-slugged"`
- `""` → throws

title: Multiline messages with markdown/rich text support
description: ## Description Support multiline messages and basic markdown rendering (bold, italic, links) in chat bubbles. Textarea instead of single-line input. ### Key Design Decision: Markdown on English Only Markdown rendering applies **only to English text**, not pig latin. Reason: pig latin transforms URLs and link text, breaking markdown links entirely. Example: `[click here](https://example.com)` → `[ickclay erehay](ttpshay://example.omcay)` — broken URL. Bold/italic markers survive transformation but applying markdown to pig latin adds complexity for no user value (pig latin is already hard to read). Rendering by context: - **Own messages** (always English): render markdown - **Explorer mode** (English subtitle): render markdown on English line; pig latin line stays plain with consonant highlights - **Detective mode** (pig latin + tap-to-reveal): no markdown (pig latin is primary) - **Spy mode** (pig latin only): no markdown ### Implementation **chat-input.tsx:** - Replace `` with `

title: Emoji reactions on messages
description:
## Description

Tap/long-press a message to add emoji reactions (thumbs up, heart, laugh, etc). Show reaction counts under the message bubble. Broadcast reactions to all room members in real-time.

### Implementation

**types.ts:**
- Add `reactions` field to `ChatMessage`: `Record<string, string[]>` (emoji -> array of usernames), default `{}`
- Define `REACTION_EMOJIS` constant: `["thumbs-up", "heart", "laugh", "wow", "sad", "party"]` with emoji mapping
- Kid-friendly curated set, no custom emoji input
- Max reactions per message per user: 1 of each emoji (toggle on/off)

**server.ts:**
- New socket events:
  - `add-reaction` `{ messageId: string, emoji: string }` -- add username to reaction map, broadcast
  - `remove-reaction` `{ messageId: string, emoji: string }` -- remove username, broadcast
- Store reactions in SQLite: new `reactions` table (`message_id TEXT, emoji TEXT, username TEXT, UNIQUE(message_id, emoji, username)`)
- On `message-history`, join reactions into each message via SQL JOIN
- Validate: emoji must be in REACTION_EMOJIS set, messageId must exist in current room buffer
- Validate: messageId must NOT be a system message (ids starting with "system-")
- Broadcast `reaction-update { messageId, reactions }` to entire room on change

**socket-context.tsx:**
- Expose `addReaction(messageId: string, emoji: string)` and `removeReaction(messageId: string, emoji: string)`
- Listen for `reaction-update` events -> merge updated reactions into the specific message in state (without re-fetching full history)

**message-bubble.tsx:**
- **System messages (username="") have NO reaction UI** -- no tap handler, no reaction bar
- Below message content: reaction bar showing each emoji + count (e.g. "thumbs-up 2  heart 1")
- Tap a reaction badge to toggle own reaction (add if not yours, remove if already reacted)
- Tap message (or "+" button on message) -> open reaction picker overlay
- Reaction picker: horizontal row of REACTION_EMOJIS, tap to select, dismiss on selection or tap-outside
- Own reactions highlighted (filled/colored background vs outline/muted)
- No reactions -> no bar shown (clean default)

**chat-room.tsx:**
- Wire `addReaction`/`removeReaction` from socket context through to MessageBubble props
- Pass current username so bubble can determine which reactions are "own"

### Unit Tests (`src/lib/reactions.test.ts`)

- Reaction map: adding username to emoji key works
- Reaction map: removing username works
- Toggle logic: same user + same emoji twice -> net removal
- Multiple users reacting same emoji -> both usernames in array
- Unknown emoji string rejected (not in REACTION_EMOJIS)
- Empty reactions map -> no crash
- System message ID (starting with "system-") -> reaction rejected

### E2E Tests (`e2e/reactions.test.ts`)

- User A sends message -> reacts thumbs-up -> reaction badge appears under message with count 1
- User B sees User A reaction appear in real-time (no refresh needed)
- User B also reacts thumbs-up -> count updates to 2 for both users
- User A taps own thumbs-up again -> removed, count drops to 1
- User A adds heart -> second emoji badge appears alongside thumbs-up
- Reaction picker opens on message tap and closes on selection
- Reaction picker closes on tap-outside without adding reaction
- System messages (join/leave) have no reaction UI -- verify no picker opens on tap
- Message history on rejoin preserves all reactions
- Reactions visible in all 3 difficulty modes (Explorer, Detective, Spy)

### Logging

- E2E: `test.step()` for each action (open picker, select, verify count update)
- Log: reaction event payload (messageId, emoji, username)
- Screenshot: after reaction added, after removed, picker open state

## Exit Condition

cd /Users/thom/10-19_projects/upidstay

grep -qE "add-reaction\|remove-reaction" server.ts

# Reactions table in DB

title: E2E test infrastructure with Playwright
description:
## Description

Set up Playwright as the e2e test framework and @testing-library/react for component tests. Create reusable test helpers and fixtures so every feature bead can include tests that actually run.

### Installation

**E2E (Playwright):**
- `pnpm add -D @playwright/test`
- `npx playwright install chromium` (only chromium needed -- single browser target)

**Component tests (React Testing Library):**
- `pnpm add -D @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom @testing-library/user-event jsdom`
- Update `vitest.config.ts` (or vite.config section): add `test.environment: 'jsdom'` for component test files

**package.json scripts:**
- `test:e2e` -- run all e2e tests
- `test:e2e:headed` -- debug mode (headed browser)
- `test:e2e:ui` -- Playwright UI mode

### Playwright Config (`playwright.config.ts`)

Use Playwright built-in `webServer` -- do NOT write a manual startDevServer helper:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  testDir: './e2e',
  timeout: 30_000,
  retries: 1,
  use: {
    baseURL: 'http://localhost:3099',
    screenshot: 'only-on-failure',
    trace: 'on-first-retry',
  },
  projects: [{ name: 'chromium', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'] } }],
  reporter: [['html'], ['list']],
  webServer: {
    command: 'pnpm run dev -- -p 3099',
    port: 3099,
    reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI,
    env: { DB_PATH: 'data/test-chat.db' },  // Isolated test DB
  },
});
```

Key decisions:
- Port 3099 avoids conflict with dev (3000) and prod (3080)
- `DB_PATH: 'data/test-chat.db'` isolates test data from dev/prod database
- `reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI` for fast local iteration
- Single chromium project (target audience uses Chrome/Chromebooks)

### Test Helpers (`e2e/helpers.ts`)

All helpers use `test.step()` for Playwright trace clarity and log timestamps:

- `joinRoom(page, { username, room, avatarId? })` -- fill join form fields, click join button, wait for chat room to load (verify message input visible). Log each step.
- `sendMessage(page, text)` -- type in message input, click send (or press Enter), wait for own message to appear in bubble list. Log text sent.
- `waitForMessage(page, { text?, from?, timeout? })` -- wait for a message matching criteria to appear. Default timeout 5s.
- `getMessages(page)` -- return array of `{ username, text, isOwn }` from current bubble list by querying DOM.
- `getReactionCounts(page, messageIndex)` -- return reaction emoji+count map for a message (used by reactions bead).

### Fixtures (`e2e/fixtures.ts`)

Extend Playwright `test` via `test.extend()`:

- `chatPage` fixture -- single user already joined a room (random room name to avoid collisions), ready to send messages
- `twoUserChat` fixture -- two separate browser contexts, both joined to the same room with different usernames. Returns `{ pageA, pageB, room }`. Both see each other in user list before fixture yields.

### Smoke Tests (`e2e/smoke.test.ts`)

Baseline tests that verify the app works at all:
- Join room, send message, see own message in bubble
- Two users join same room, User A sends message, User B sees it in real-time
- Typing indicator: User A types, User B sees "A is typing..."
- User disconnect: User A leaves, User B sees "A left" system message
- Room list: after joining, room appears in room list with user count

### Gitignore Additions

Add to `.gitignore`:
```
playwright-report/
test-results/
e2e/logs/
data/test-chat.db
```

### Test Convention Note

**Unit/component test files:** colocated with source (e.g. `src/lib/foo.test.ts`) -- matches existing convention (`pig-latin.test.ts`, `slugify.test.ts`, `share.test.ts`).

**E2E test files:** in `e2e/` directory (e.g. `e2e/smoke.test.ts`).

### Logging Requirements

- Every helper function logs entry/exit with `console.log` timestamps
- Failed assertions include page screenshot (Playwright default with `screenshot: 'only-on-failure'`)
- Browser console logs captured and attached to test report via `page.on('console')`
- Playwright HTML report generated on every run

## Exit Condition

```bash
set -e
cd /Users/thom/10-19_projects/upidstay

# Playwright installed and configured
test -f playwright.config.ts
pnpm list @playwright/test | grep -q playwright

# React Testing Library installed
pnpm list @testing-library/react | grep -q testing-library

# Test scripts in package.json
grep -q "test:e2e" package.json

# Helpers and fixtures exist
test -f e2e/helpers.ts
test -f e2e/fixtures.ts

# Smoke tests exist and use helpers
grep -qE "joinRoom|sendMessage" e2e/smoke.test.ts

# Playwright uses webServer config (not manual server management)
grep -qE "webServer" playwright.config.ts

# Test DB isolation configured
grep -qE "test-chat" playwright.config.ts

# Gitignore updated
grep -q "playwright-report" .gitignore
grep -q "test-chat" .gitignore

# Build passes
pnpm build

# Unit tests still pass
pnpm test

# E2E smoke tests pass
pnpm test:e2e --reporter=list 2>&1 | tee /tmp/e2e-smoke.log
grep -qE "passed" /tmp/e2e-smoke.log
rm -f /tmp/e2e-smoke.log

echo "bd-yma verified"
```
